title: Partner co-marketing plan — Benchmark Report launch (latency/$ economics)
content:
Owner: Noura
Last working session: 2025-06-26 (partner sync)

Goal
Use cloud + ISV partners to amplify the Benchmark Report launch beyond Redwood-owned channels, with clear timing, approved messaging, and measurable attribution.

Primary outcomes
1) Drive incremental qualified traffic to the benchmark landing page + interactive table.
2) Increase developer signups (Hosted API) and demo requests (Dedicated/Private) via partner distribution.
3) Build credibility via “third-party distribution” (NOT third-party endorsement) while keeping claims compliant.

Non-goals / guardrails
- No partner content should imply the partner validated Redwood’s measurements.
- Avoid “best/fastest/cheapest” absolute claims in partner channels.
- Any comparative or competitor-referencing language must match Legal-approved phrasing.
- Partners can share Redwood assets; partners should not create their own charts/numbers.

Launch assumptions (tentative)
- Target public launch date (T0): 2025-07-15 (Tue) 
- Embargo for pre-briefs / partner prep: T0 - 7 days (2025-07-08)
- Partner content window: T0 through T0 + 10 business days

Target partner categories & proposed plays
A) Cloud providers / marketplaces
1) Marketplace listing tie-in (AWS/GCP/Azure)
   - Placement request: “What’s new” or “Featured listings” (best effort)
   - CTA: “Deploy Redwood Inference → View Benchmark Report → Start free credits”
   - Asset: short marketplace-friendly blurb + approved hero image
   - Timing: submit request by T0 - 10 business days

2) Cloud partner newsletter snippet
   - Format: 80–120 words + 1 link + optional image
   - Angle: “Benchmark report on inference economics (latency/$) across regions; methodology + interactive results.”
   - Timing: target week-of-launch issue; if newsletter cycle misses, place in next issue with “new report” framing.

3) Partner blog cross-post (syndication) OR partner resource hub listing
   - If full blog slot isn’t available, ask for resource hub placement with a short summary.
   - Content source of truth remains Redwood blog + landing page.

B) ISVs / developer platforms (integration adjacency)
1) Co-branded “how to read the benchmark” short post (lightweight)
   - Goal: educational framing; avoid product wars.
   - Minimal lift for partner: we provide draft; partner adds intro/outro + link.
   - Timing: publish T0 + 2 to T0 + 7 days.

2) Newsletter placements (ISV weekly digests)
   - Format: short blurb + link (UTM’d)
   - Prefer partners with strong developer audience reach.

3) Social amplification kit (1–2 posts + visual)
   - Provide partner with:
     - Approved copy variants (X/LinkedIn)
     - 1 static image (chart teaser with disclaimer) + 1 product screenshot (interactive table)
     - Tracking links
   - Timing: Day 0 and Day 3 recommended.

C) Webinar / live event support
1) Partner “guest appearance” (low-risk)
   - Partner joins for 5-minute intro on why inference economics matters + closing plug (no validation of results).
   - Redwood owns methodology + data talk.
   - Timing: webinar scheduled for T0 + 7–10 days.

2) Partner community calendar listing
   - If partner runs events calendar, list Redwood webinar.

Proposed partner short-list (working)
NOTE: final list depends on partner responsiveness + compliance comfort.
- Cloud marketplaces: AWS Marketplace, Google Cloud Marketplace, Azure Marketplace (requests in parallel)
- Infra/Dev platforms: Vercel (newsletter/resource hub), Cloudflare (developer newsletter), Datadog (community/newsletter)
- LLM ecosystem/ISVs: (TBD based on existing relationships; keep to “distribution” not “endorsement”)

Approved core message for partners (draft copy blocks)
Short (1–2 sentences)
“Redwood Inference published a new benchmark report focused on production inference economics—latency and cost efficiency (latency/$) across models and regions—with a detailed methodology and interactive results.”

Slightly longer (80–120 words)
“Redwood Inference just released a benchmark report on production inference economics, focusing on latency and cost efficiency (latency/$) across a curated set of LLMs and deployment regions. The report includes a transparent methodology, reproducible artifacts, and an interactive table so teams can explore results by model and region. If you’re building LLM features in production, it’s a practical reference for thinking about throughput, p95 latency, and cost per 1M tokens.”

Required disclaimer line (include when space allows)
“Results reflect Redwood’s measured configurations and workloads; performance varies by prompt mix, concurrency, and region. See methodology for details.”

Linking + tracking
- All partner links must use UTMs per Tyler/Ben’s conventions.
- Base links:
  - Landing page: /benchmarks/latency-per-dollar
  - PDF report: /benchmarks/latency-per-dollar/report.pdf
  - Methodology: /benchmarks/latency-per-dollar/methodology
- UTM convention (proposal):
  - utm_source={partner_slug}
  - utm_medium={newsletter|blog|social|marketplace|webinar}
  - utm_campaign=benchmark_report_launch_2025
  - utm_content={placement_name}

Deliverables we need to hand partners (asset kit)
1) “Partner press kit mini” (single folder)
   - 1–2 approved social images (with disclaimer text baked in)
   - 1 product screenshot of interactive table
   - 2–3 pre-written social copy variants
   - 1 newsletter blurb (short + long)
   - 1 marketplace blurb (50–80 words)
   - Link list (UTM’d) + do/don’t language
Owner: Soojin (copy) + Ethan (blog snippet) + Alicia (visuals) + Tyler (UTMs)

2) Webinar invite block
   - Title, abstract, speaker list, registration link, 2 bullets on what attendees get
Owner: Noura

3) FAQ snippet for partner teams
   - “Are you claiming partner validation?” (No)
   - “Can we share charts?” (Only Redwood-provided images)
   - “How should we respond to fairness questions?” (Point to methodology)
Owner: Soojin (align with Legal)

Timing & workback (draft)
T0 = 2025-07-15

By T0 - 14 days (2025-07-01)
- Confirm which partner channels we’re pursuing + primary contacts (Noura)
- Provide partners with embargo language + draft snippets (Soojin)
- Confirm landing page URL + final naming (Soojin/Wei)

By T0 - 10 business days
- Submit marketplace placement requests (Noura)
- Create UTMs + tracking sheet (Tyler/Ben)

By T0 - 7 days (embargo start)
- Share final partner kit folder (copy + visuals) (Soojin/Ethan/Alicia)
- Provide “approved responses” for common questions (Soojin)

T0 (launch day)
- Partner social posts wave 1 (coordinated, optional)
- Marketplace listing update live (if approved)

T0 + 3 days
- Partner social wave 2 (optional)
- Newsletter placements (dependent on cycles)

T0 + 7–10 days
- Webinar (partner cameo optional)
- Partner resource hub / blog syndication (if available)

Measurement plan (minimum)
1) Traffic + conversions
- Sessions to landing page by utm_source/medium
- CTA clicks: “Start free credits” and “Talk to sales” from benchmark page
- PDF downloads

2) Pipeline influence (enterprise motion)
- HubSpot campaign association: benchmark_report_launch_2025
- Track partner-sourced demo requests separately from Redwood-owned channels

3) Qualitative signals
- Inbound mentions: “saw this via {partner}” captured by SDR/AEs
- Community feedback and external commentary (supporting credibility)

Risks & mitigations
1) Risk: Partner asks for stronger comparative language
   - Mitigation: Provide strict do/don’t list; escalate to Michael/Sofia if needed.

2) Risk: Partner wants to edit or recreate charts
   - Mitigation: Only allow Redwood-provided images; no recharting.

3) Risk: Newsletter deadlines missed
   - Mitigation: Have “launch week” and “post-launch (new report)” versions ready.

4) Risk: Partner content implies endorsement
   - Mitigation: Mandatory language: “Redwood published…” and “see methodology…”; remove any “validated by” phrasing.

Open questions (need answers)
- Which marketplaces are live for Redwood today, and what update process/SLAs apply? (Need Felix/Wei + partnerships contact)
- Final list of regions/models that are “supported for publication” vs “experimental” (Henry + Jonas)
- Can we offer a partner-specific promo (e.g., extra credits) without creating fairness concerns? (Ben + Legal)
- Webinar: do we want a partner co-host, or just distribution? (Camila + Soojin)

Action items (as of 2025-06-28)
- Noura: draft partner outreach email + propose embargo terms (due 2025-07-01)
- Soojin: finalize partner-safe copy blocks + disclaimer line (due 2025-07-02)
- Ethan: provide 150-word “what’s in the report” snippet for partner blogs (due 2025-07-03)
- Tyler/Ben: confirm UTM naming + reporting view for partner channels (due 2025-07-03)
- Camila: approve final partner list + priority (due 2025-07-02)

Notes from 2025-06-26 partner sync (high-level)
- Partners are generally open to newsletter/resource-hub distribution if we keep it educational and avoid direct competitor callouts.
- Marketplace teams need final URLs and a short approved description; lead times vary.
- Recommendation: keep partner requests lightweight (newsletter + social) unless we have a strong mutual customer story (we do not yet for this launch).
